title: Explicit ref-locking and timebound resolution for serving (tag, semver, hash)
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Define and implement deterministic reference-locking semantics for model references used by clients (tag, semver range, commit-hash, and ephemeral tags) with optional timebound (TTL) resolution and explicit fallback behavior. This ticket captures API surface decisions, runtime resolver changes, migration guardrails, and telemetry required to make model selection predictable for customers across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
background: Current resolver behavior allows flexible selectors (tags, aliases, semver ranges) but has led to surprising rollouts where a tag mutated and a customer traffic spike hit a new model variant. We need a clear contract that supports: (1) stable pinned references, (2) friendly developer workflows (pin by tag or semver during dev), and (3) operational escape hatches (timebound locks, ephemeral pins). Runtime currently supports hash-based exact selection and tag lookup but lacks a standardized TTL/locking layer and API to express fallbacks.
proposal: Introduce 'ref_lock' API field and client SDK helpers that allow callers to request resolution modes: exact (hash), anchored (tag+lock_ttl), semver_range (with anchor option), and ephemeral (no anchor). Server-side resolver will return a resolution object with resolved_ref, resolved_at, lock_expires_at (if applicable), and a stability_score hint. Add explicit fallback rules: user-provided fallback_ref(s) (ordered) and a runtime policy for auto-degradation (e.g., fallback to a compatible quantized variant). Document semantics for timebound locks: a lock is a promise that the same resolved_ref will be returned for the duration unless operator-initiated emergency rollbacks occur (and those must emit outage-level telemetry).
tradeoffs: Pros: predictable inference behavior for customers, safer rollouts, easier postmortems. Cons: added complexity in the resolver API, additional state to track (locks) and edge cases around cross-region consistency and cache invalidation. Timebound locks may delay critical security fixes unless operators can invalidate locks; we will add an emergency invalidation signal with audit logs. Anchoring by tag improves developer ergonomics but requires educating users about when to anchor versus rely on floating tags.
acceptance_criteria: API: SDK and REST surfaces accept 'ref_lock' with fields {mode, ttl_seconds, fallback_refs} and return a standardized resolution response
Runtime: resolver honors ttl-based anchors and returns identical resolved_ref for duration unless invalidated by operator action
Fallbacks: when primary resolved_ref is unavailable, runtime consults ordered fallback_refs and documents policy in Console
Telemetry: metrics emitted for resolution decisions (resolved_ref, mode, hit_fallback, invalidation_event) and tracing spans link request->resolution
Migration: existing clients without ref_lock continue to resolve using current semantics; we provide server-side opt-in to enforce strict-anchoring per-tenant
Docs: Confluence spec, SDK docs, and Console UI mockups published and linked
implementation_plan: API: add 'ref_lock' to model request payload and SDK helper in JS/Python (ENG-API work)
Resolver: extend resolver to store temporary anchor entries in the cluster metadata store with TTL and provide admin invalidation endpoint
Runtime: ensure cache keys include resolved_ref and lock metadata to prevent stale cache returns
Fallbacks: implement ordered fallback resolution policy with circuit-breaker heuristics
Telemetry: emit 'model_resolution' event with fields {client_id, selector, resolved_ref, mode, ttl, fallback_used, reason}
Tests: unit tests for resolver logic, integration tests across regions to validate cross-region TTL consistency
SDK: add convenience 'pin()' helper to generate ref_lock payloads for common workflows
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): server-side opt-in for specific orgs; SDK flag to enable explicit ref_lock calls; collect telemetry and feedback
Phase 2 (scale): enable ref_lock by default for new tenants and provide migration tool to suggest anchors based on historical resolution stability
Phase 3 (enforcement): Console option to require strict anchoring for a tenant; document and run communications plan for enterprise customers
telemetry_and_alerting: New telemetry events: model_resolution.start, model_resolution.end, model_resolution.fallback_used, model_resolution.invalidation
Dashboards: resolution mode breakdown, fallback rate by tenant, increased invalidation/rollback alerts
Alerts: high fallback rate (>1% of requests) or mismatch between resolved_ref and runtime-serving artifact (indicates cache/inconsistency)
Retention: wire resolution events to S3/log store for 90 days for postmortems
compatibility_migration: Backwards compatibility: existing requests w/o ref_lock keep current behavior
Migration helper: 'suggest_anchor' endpoint that analyzes past 30-day selection stability and recommends anchor candidates
Cross-version: ensure older SDKs get 400 with guidance if tenant has strict anchoring enforced
Private deployment notes: provide operator-run script to enable anchor metadata replication between control-plane and private control-plane instances
security_considerations: Anchor metadata is sensitive operational state; restrict admin invalidation to RBAC role 'model-admin' and audit all invalidations
Lock TTLs should reject excessively long values (>180 days) unless tenant is enterprise with signed approval
Ensure resolution events exclude any customer prompt content; only metadata about selectors and refs are emitted
